blocks.title: Agile methodology
blocks.text: Agile methodology is a flexible and adaptive approach to software development. Unlike the Waterfall model, which follows a strict sequence of steps, Agile delivers small, working parts of the software quickly and adapts to changes as the project progresses, working in short cycles called iterations or sprints and gathering feedback early (Fig. 1.3).

items: Continuous integration: regularly merging code changes into a central repository to detect and fix issues early.
Test-driven development: writing tests before writing the code so the software works as expected.
Pair programming: two developers at one workstation, one writing code and the other reviewing it in real time.

blocks.caption: Agile: benefits and limitations
rows: High flexibility: requirements can change even after development has started
Scaling challenges: large projects with many teams need careful coordination
Improved customer satisfaction: frequent working releases let customers see progress and give feedback
Stakeholder involvement: needs active participation from all stakeholders
Less predictable: timeline and final scope are harder to predict

blocks.prompt: Which model involves working in short cycles or sprints (MCQ 4)? Illustrate continuous integration in Agile and its importance (short question 3).
blocks.explanation: Agile methodology, option (b). In continuous integration each developer merges small code changes into the shared repository several times a day, and automated builds and tests run on each merge; conflicts and bugs are caught while they are small, so the team always has working, tested code.

blocks.prompt: You manage a simple mobile app project. How would you use Agile (long question 2)?
blocks.explanation: List the features as a prioritized backlog; plan short sprints of one to two weeks, each building and testing a few features; integrate code continuously and test it; show the working app to the client at the end of each sprint, take feedback and re-plan; repeat until the app is ready, then release and keep improving it.

items: Agile: flexible, adaptive; short iterations or sprints delivering small working parts with early feedback (Fig. 1.3).
Practices: continuous integration, test-driven development, pair programming. Benefits: flexibility, customer satisfaction; limits: scaling, stakeholder involvement, less predictable.
